$comment: Ground truth for the eval suite: ten shipments, one row each, as supplied
by Meridian. This is the expected_output shape the generated agent must
Discipline (Claude.md §9): the SHAPE of this file informs the reviewer's
questions; the VALUES are the repair loop's oracle. Deriving business rules
from these numbers and encoding them directly fits the spec to the test set
rather than to the process. Anything inferred here is a hypothesis to put to
the process owner, never an answer.
Column names are verbatim from the source table, including the one that
misnames its own unit — see notes.mismatched_asn_unit.
unit: one row per shipment, not per email and not per invoice

notes.two_columns_are_sums: invoices_successful + invoices_failed == invoices_total, and coa_success + failed_coa == coa_total, on 10 of 10 rows. Neither total is configured anywhere: an invoice enumerates the batches, so coa_total is derived from what arrived rather than from a count somebody set. A generated agent that emits a total it did not derive is guessing.
notes.invoices_per_shipment: 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 1, 3, 7, 3, 11 — one row can span eleven invoices, so a shipment is many emails and many documents. This is the correlation requirement, stated as data.
notes.mismatched_asn_unit: MNBU3974949 reports 1 invoice and 14 mismatched ASN; MNBU4371364 reports 3 and 9; CGMU5630052 reports 1 and 2. Three rows where the count exceeds the invoice count, so the column named 'Invoices (Mismatched ASN)' is not counting invoices. Most likely line items. A question for the process owner, not something to infer.
notes.asn_does_not_block: All three shipments with ASN mismatches (14, 9, 2) are RESOLVED, and no ACTIVE row has any. ASN mismatch is non-blocking. Settles Claude.md §8's open item on three independent data points.
notes.asn_has_no_source_in_the_spec: There is no ASN entity, no ASN check and no ASN field on the frozen board, so nothing can produce this column. The likely source is the per-invoice .xlsx attachments in the mailbox — one spreadsheet per invoice number. That is a round-2 corpus-grounded finding for the reviewer, not something codegen may invent.
notes.goods_is_line_items_and_an_invoice_fails: The two rows with goods_failed > 0 are the only two with invoices_failed > 0: CAAU4056270 has 2 goods / 1 invoice, MNBU3852977 has 6 goods / 3 invoices. Goods counts line items, an invoice fails when any of its line items does, and the same check therefore reports at two grains. Exactly the case domain.Fill was written for.
notes.status_follows_the_unresolved_discrepanc: ACTIVE on every row where goods_failed or failed_coa is non-zero; RESOLVED otherwise, with ASN excluded. Fits 10 of 10. MCAU6047165 is the decisive row: all 11 invoices pass and it is still ACTIVE, on a single failed COA — so status tracks any open discrepancy rather than invoice completeness alone. Strong enough for codegen to implement and for the sweep to falsify; still a hypothesis, because only the process owner can say what closes a shipment and the SOP ends at 'report the discrepancy'.
notes.identifier_kind_varies: Nine rows are ISO container numbers; 176-26926281 is an air waybill. The shipment key depends on mode of transport, which the SOP never mentions. Both forms appear in the mail subject line — 'Container No: MNBU0458316' and 'MAWB:020-07721814' — so the correlation key is recoverable without opening an attachment.
notes.176_26926281_is_not_in_the_mailbox: Verified against the live inbox on 2026-08-17: 14 messages, 11 distinct shipments, and this key appears in none of them. The row has no input, so it is carried as split=holdout and excluded from the denominator rather than counted as nine permanent failures. Named here so the gap is documented rather than silently absorbed.
notes.the_mailbox_holds_more_than_the_eval_set: Two shipments in the inbox are scored by no row — container MNBU0458316 and air waybill 020-07721814. An agent that processes everything it finds is not wrong, but the suite measures nine of the eleven, and a sweep reporting eleven rows has miscounted rather than over-delivered.
